Choisis une question, écris tes chiffres: Choose a question, enter your numbers, read the answer, then save whatever helps you decide. You can change the Tutorial examples. No number here is an official in-game price or earnings figure.
<1>Dis d’où tu pars.</1> « J’ai déjà »,: <1>Tell it where you’re starting from.</1> “I already have” is the money you have now. “Money I set aside” is what you don’t want to spend.
<1>Dis comment tu gagnes.</1> Soit petit: <1>Tell it how you earn.</1> Either bit by bit, per hour of play, or at the end of each mission.
<1>Vérifie et garde.</1> Les cases sont: <1>Check and keep.</1> The fields are the same from one tool to the next. “☆ Save this calculation” stores your try in “My calculations”.
Ces chiffres iront dans ton calcul en co: These numbers will go into your current calculation. If you already have a calculation in progress, save it before loading this exercise.
Sur petit écran, les outils sont rangés: On small screens, the tools are laid out in two columns. On a keyboard, the left and right arrows move from one tool to the next. The “Back to the Tutorial chapter” link takes you back to where you started.
Les trois modes donnent la même réponse: The three modes give the same answer with the same numbers: they only change how you fill things in and read them. <1>Simple</1> shows the answer sentence, the numbers behind it and your next step; the rest (“What matters in this calculation”, the trade-off, the formula) is tucked into collapsed sections: tap a section to open it, and you can change each assumption in one click. <2>Step by step</2> asks one question at a time, explains why it’s asking and skips the ones that no longer matter (for example when your goal is already reached). <3>Expert</3> adds every setting (fees, cooldown, share…), the tables, the curves (with clickable points), the thresholds, the explanations and the comparison with a saved calculation, also in collapsible sections. The business plan has its three modes too.
« Ce qui compte dans ce calcul » dit en: “What matters in this calculation” sums up in one line what decided the answer. Its details (“Full details: conditions, numbers, ruled-out criteria”) have six parts: what the calculation is looking for and over what period, the required conditions, the numbers used (each with its source or status), what decides the answer, what would change the answer, and the ruled-out criteria, each with its reason. It’s built from the criteria actually used for your situation.
Changer de mode garde tes chiffres. Un r: Switching modes keeps your numbers. A setting changed in Expert mode still counts in Simple: a “Changed in Expert mode” line says so above the tool. Each tool keeps its own mode.

Commence ici. Tu dis combien tu as, comb: Start here. You say how much you have, how much you want and what you earn: the calculator tells you how much play time you need and in how many days you’ll get there.
Quatre cases : « J’ai déjà », « Je veux: Four fields: “I already have”, “I want to have”, “I earn about ($ per hour of play)” and “I play every day”. The quick buttons and the slider save you from typing.
« Mon objectif, c’est » : de l’argent en: “My goal is”: extra money on top of what I set aside, the money I’ll have in total, or what I’ll earn from now on. Then “Money set aside, expenses, deadline”: the money I set aside, the purchases to pay before my goal, what I spend each session (consumables, ammo…) and “I want to get there in (days)”. Also “Which activity gets me to my goal fastest?”, “What if the number moves by 20%?” and “Compare with a saved calculation”.

Le sens de ton but change la cible : « e: What your goal means changes the target: “on top of what I set aside” adds your reserve, “in total” counts it in, “from now on” doesn’t count what you already have. Choisis une voiture, une arme, un lieu o: Choose a car, a weapon, a place or a business from the site, or enter a price. The calculator tells you whether you can buy it now, and if not, how much play time you need.
Deux étapes : « Quel est ton achat ? » (: Two steps: “What’s your purchase?” (name and price) and “How much do you have?” (what you have, what you set aside). What you earn and your goal are extras, if you want.
« À quoi il te sert ? », « Il coûte quel: “What do you use it for?”, “Does it cost something each session?” (“It costs me each session” and “I use it for (sessions)”), “How long to earn back this price?”. In Expert: “Options I take”, “Required upfront fees”, “I could resell it” (your assumption, never counted in today’s money), “Its capabilities, if you know them” (where it can go, seats), “Does this purchase make me money?”, “What if the number moves by 20%?” and “Compare with a saved calculation”.
Pouvoir payer maintenant et pouvoir teni: Being able to pay now and being able to keep it up are two separate answers: the price, the options and the required fees must fit in the money available (what you have minus what you set aside); a cost each session can make the purchase impossible to keep up after a few sessions, and the answer says so. A vehicle or weapon already checked in “My garage” or “My arsenal” comes in as “already owned”: nothing to pay, and you can uncheck “Purchase already owned” to buy another one.
